description.text: The promos of the Diamond & Pearl Series, DP01 to DP56, released from May 2007 to December 2009: the first Black Star Promos with a prefix in their number. Nearly all came in products. Two- and three-pack blisters of each expansion carried the plainer cards, while collector's tins carried LV.X promos, from the Sinnoh first partners' final forms to Dialga, Palkia, Darkrai, Giratina, Shaymin and Arceus. Others came in value packs, premium boxes, poster packs and the Platinum Player's Guide, and the trophy card Tropical Wind went to players at the 2007, 2008 and 2009 World Championships. Two Trainer cards, Beginning Door and Ultimate Zone (DP54 and DP55), are known only in French.

tell.text: A black star promo symbol and a "DP" number at the bottom right

description.text: The first of the Diamond & Pearl Black Star Promos, a holofoil Turtwig sold in a Diamond & Pearl three-pack blister in 2007. Three such blisters each held one of the Sinnoh starter Pokémon: Turtwig, Chimchar DP02 and Piplup DP03. Masakazu Fukuda's art first came in Japan as Turtwig 005/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's February 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

A holofoil Chimchar from a Diamond & Pearl three-pack blister of 2007, one of three that each held one of the Sinnoh starter Pokémon, with Turtwig DP01 and Piplup DP03. Announced in May 2007 for a June release, the Chimchar blister held two Diamond & Pearl booster packs, an EX Power Keepers pack and a Palkia coin. Kagemaru Himeno's art first came in Japan as Chimchar 007/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's February 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

A holofoil Piplup from a Diamond & Pearl three-pack blister of 2007, one of three that each held one of the Sinnoh starter Pokémon, with Turtwig DP01 and Chimchar DP02. Atsuko Nishida's art first came in Japan as Piplup 008/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's February 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

A holofoil Pachirisu from a Diamond & Pearl two-pack blister of 2007. Atsuko Nishida's art first came in Japan as Pachirisu 011/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's February 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

Tropical Wind returned as the promo card of the 2007 Pokémon World Championships, held from 10 to 12 August 2007 at the Hilton Waikoloa Village in Hawaii, keeping Sumiyoshi Kizuki's Psyduck artwork. Every competitor received the card in seven languages (English, Japanese, Spanish, Italian, German, French and Portuguese), each stamped "WORLDS 07", in a nine-pocket binder page.

The trophy versions carry a placement stamp, from Top Thirty-Two up to Finalist, and staff got a Staff copy. In all there were thirteen versions of the 2007 card.

description.text: The 2007 Finalist copy of Tropical Wind, the highest stamp of 2007, given to players who reached that stage at the World Championships in Hawaii. According to Elite Fourum's organized-play timeline, 6 were awarded.

description.text: The 2007 Tropical Wind, given to every player of the trading card game at the start of the 2007 World Championships, in a nine-card collection: the card in seven languages, a card advertising the next World Championship Decks and one with the date and venue of the next World Championships.

A holofoil Buneary sold at Target from September 2007 in a Mysterious Treasures two-pack blister with one Mysterious Treasures and one POP Series 3 booster pack; the same blister came with Cranidos DP07 instead. Kagemaru Himeno's art first came in Japan as Buneary 015/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's February 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

A holofoil Cranidos sold at Target from September 2007 in two Mysterious Treasures blisters: a two-pack with one Mysterious Treasures and one POP Series 3 booster pack, which also came with Buneary DP06, and a three-pack with two Mysterious Treasures packs and one EX series pack, which also came with Shieldon DP08.

A holofoil Shieldon sold at Target from September 2007 in a Mysterious Treasures three-pack blister with two Mysterious Treasures booster packs, one EX series pack and a Shieldon coin. The same blister also came with Cranidos DP07.

One of three Diamond & Pearl Collector's Tins released in September 2007, each with four Diamond & Pearl series booster packs and a holofoil LV.X of a Sinnoh starter's final form: Torterra LV.X here, Infernape LV.X DP10 and Empoleon LV.X DP11. All three reprint the Diamond & Pearl set's LV.X cards with new art by Shizurow, which reached Japan only later: this Torterra LV.X became promo 076/DP-P, in a New Year special pack of January 2008 with a new Bronzong promo, two Diamond & Pearl packs and one Secret of the Lakes pack.

One of three Diamond & Pearl Collector's Tins released in September 2007, each with four Diamond & Pearl series booster packs and a holofoil LV.X of a Sinnoh starter's final form: Infernape LV.X here, Torterra LV.X DP09 and Empoleon LV.X DP11. All three reprint the Diamond & Pearl set's LV.X cards with new art by Shizurow, which reached Japan only later: this Infernape LV.X became promo 071/DP-P, a participation prize at the Winter Challenge tournaments of November 2007.

One of three Diamond & Pearl Collector's Tins released in September 2007, each with four Diamond & Pearl series booster packs and a holofoil LV.X of a Sinnoh starter's final form: Empoleon LV.X here, Torterra LV.X DP09 and Infernape LV.X DP10. All three reprint the Diamond & Pearl set's LV.X cards with new art by Shizurow, which reached Japan only later: this Empoleon LV.X became promo 078/DP-P, in a New Year special pack of January 2008 with a new Mothim promo, two Diamond & Pearl packs and one Shining Darkness pack.

The holofoil Lucario LV.X from the Lucario tin, released in November 2007 at stores such as Target and Toys R Us with three Secret Wonders booster packs and one Mysterious Treasures pack. It reprints the Mysterious Treasures Lucario LV.X with different art: Ryo Ueda's drawing, which first came in Japan as promo 004/DP-P with the official visual book of the Space-Time Creation set in December 2006.

A holofoil Buizel sold from November 2007 at stores such as Target and Wal-Mart in a blister with a holofoil reprint of POP Series 6 Gible. Chatot DP14 came the same week in a similar blister with a holofoil POP Series 6 Pikachu. Mitsuhiro Arita's art first came in Japan as Buizel 009/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's February 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

A holofoil Chatot sold from November 2007 at stores such as Target and Wal-Mart in a blister with a holofoil reprint of POP Series 6 Pikachu, one Mysterious Treasures and three Secret Wonders booster packs, and a blue or red Energy coin. Buizel DP13 came the same week in a similar blister with a holofoil POP Series 6 Gible. In Japan, Masakazu Fukuda's Chatot was a non-holo card, 016/DP-P, one of twelve in Meiji's February 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

A holofoil Shinx from the Diamond & Pearl Trainer's Challenge Set, in stores by the end of September 2007. Outside North America it also came with Pikachu DP16 in a green DP Value Pack 2 blister. It reprints the Diamond & Pearl set's Shinx with different art: Kagemaru Himeno's drawing, which first came in Japan as Shinx 010/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's February 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

A holofoil Pikachu found from November 2007 at Wal-Mart in a blister with a Secret Wonders theme deck and a Mysterious Treasures booster pack. Outside North America it also came with Shinx DP15 in a green DP Value Pack 2 blister. It reprints the Mysterious Treasures Pikachu with different art. Sumiyoshi Kizuki's drawing was also printed in Japan on holofoil promos 048/DP-P, traded at a Trade Please DP event on 8 July 2007, and 057/DP-P, a Battle Road Summer 2007 prize. A copy with a silver snowflake stamp came in the 2008 Pokémon Countdown Calendar.

One of three LV.X tins released at the end of February 2008, each with four booster packs (one Great Encounters, one Mysterious Treasures and two Secret Wonders) and a holofoil LV.X: Dialga LV.X here, Palkia LV.X DP18 or Darkrai LV.X DP19. All three reprint the Great Encounters LV.X cards with other art. Ryo Ueda's art first came in Japan on the Dialga LV.X of the Dialga LV.X constructed standard deck, one of Japan's two Shining Darkness theme decks.

One of three LV.X tins released at the end of February 2008, each with four booster packs (one Great Encounters, one Mysterious Treasures and two Secret Wonders) and a holofoil LV.X: Palkia LV.X here, Dialga LV.X DP17 or Darkrai LV.X DP19. All three reprint the Great Encounters LV.X cards with other art. Ryo Ueda's art first came in Japan on the Palkia LV.X of the Palkia LV.X constructed standard deck, one of Japan's two Shining Darkness theme decks.

One of three LV.X tins released at the end of February 2008, each with four booster packs (one Great Encounters, one Mysterious Treasures and two Secret Wonders) and a holofoil LV.X: Darkrai LV.X here, Dialga LV.X DP17 or Palkia LV.X DP18. All three reprint the Great Encounters LV.X cards with other art. Shizurow's Darkrai art was new to cards, taken from official artwork made to promote Japan's Diamond & Pearl sets.
A holofoil Magmortar from a Great Encounters three-pack blister of March 2008, sold shortly after the set came out; Raichu DP21 came in the other.

A holofoil Raichu from a Great Encounters three-pack blister of March 2008, sold shortly after the set came out; Magmortar DP20 came in the other. It has the attacks of the Mysterious Treasures Raichu, drawn differently: Daisuke Ito's Raichu here faces the viewer.

A holofoil Mime Jr. sold from June 2008 at stores such as Target in a Majestic Dawn blister with two Majestic Dawn and one EX Dragon Frontiers booster pack and a Lucario coin; Glameow DP23 came in the same blister instead. Both reprint cards of the Diamond & Pearl set with different art. Mitsuhiro Arita's Mime Jr. first came in Japan as 021/DP-P, from a Trade Please DP event at the World Hobby Fair 2007.

A holofoil Glameow sold from June 2008 at stores such as Target in a Majestic Dawn blister with two Majestic Dawn and one EX Dragon Frontiers booster pack and a Lucario coin; Mime Jr. DP22 came in the same blister instead. Both reprint cards of the Diamond & Pearl set with different art. Mitsuhiro Arita's Glameow first came in Japan as 024/DP-P, from a Trade Please DP event at the World Hobby Fair 2007.

A holofoil Darkrai from the Darkrai Premium Box, released on 12 May 2008 with a Diamond & Pearl series theme deck, two booster packs and a jumbo copy of the card. Kouki Saitou's art first came in Japan as Darkrai 046/DP-P, handed out in cinemas showing the tenth Pokémon film, Dialga vs. Palkia vs. Darkrai, from July 2007, to complete a collection of the film's promos. In English the film is The Rise of Darkrai.

tell.text: No foil anywhere on the card.

description.text: A non-holo copy came with The Rise of Darkrai on DVD in Europe, in September 2008. It is far scarcer than the holo card.

description.text: A jumbo copy, about 8 by 5¾ inches, came in the Darkrai Premium Box with the regular card. It is holofoil too, but with a plain shine instead of the regular card's sparkles. It was the first English jumbo card since Shadow Lugia in 2005, which had been handed out only at a Pokémon XD event.

Tropical Wind was the World Championships promo again in 2008, for the tournament held from 15 to 17 August 2008 at the Hilton Orlando Lake Buena Vista in Florida. As in earlier years, competitors received the card in seven languages and staff got a Staff copy. The trophy versions carry a placement stamp from Top Thirty-Two up to Finalist, which stayed the highest stamp until a Champion stamp appeared in 2012.

A holofoil Dialga from the Dialga Premium Box, released in August 2008 with a Diamond & Pearl series theme deck, two booster packs and a jumbo copy of the card; the Palkia Premium Box held Palkia DP27. The jumbo came in either mirror or cracked ice holofoil. Both promos reprint the Dialga and Palkia of the Diamond & Pearl and Great Encounters sets with different art. Kazuyuki Kano's drawing first came in Japan as Dialga 042/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's July 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

description.text: A holofoil Palkia from the Palkia Premium Box, released in August 2008 with a Diamond & Pearl series theme deck, two booster packs and a jumbo copy of the card; the Dialga Premium Box held Dialga DP26. The jumbo came in either mirror or cracked ice holofoil. Like Dialga, it reprints the Palkia of the Diamond & Pearl and Great Encounters sets with different art. According to the product sheet PokéBeach quoted, a case held seven Dialga boxes and five Palkia boxes. Daisuke Ito's art first came in Japan as Palkia 039/DP-P, one of twelve cards in Meiji's July 2007 series of Pokémon chocolate promos.

description.text: The holofoil Mewtwo LV.X from one of two fall tins, released in September 2008, each with four booster packs; the other held Rhyperior LV.X DP29. Shizurow's art was made for the English card. It reached Japan in April 2009, on the Mewtwo LV.X of a Pokémon Card Collection pack (PtM 6).

The holofoil Rhyperior LV.X from one of two fall tins, released in September 2008, each with four booster packs; the other held Mewtwo LV.X DP28. Ryo Ueda's art was made for the English card and was not on any Japanese card at the time.

The holofoil Regigigas LV.X from one of two holiday tins, in stores from November 2008 with four booster packs; the other held Heatran LV.X DP31. Shizurow's art was made for the English card. It reached Japan in April 2009, on the Regigigas LV.X of a Pokémon Card Collection pack (PtR 11).

The holofoil Heatran LV.X from one of two holiday tins, in stores from November 2008 with four booster packs; the other held Regigigas LV.X DP30. Shizurow's art first came in Japan as Heatran LV.X 092/DP-P, packed with the official visual book of the Temple of Anger and Cry from the Mysterious sets on 14 March 2008.

A holofoil Magnezone from the Stormfront three-pack blister, released with Stormfront in November 2008 with two Stormfront booster packs, one Secret Wonders pack and a Dialga or Palkia coin. The other blister held Dusknoir DP33. Both reached stores in other countries first and only trickled into American shops in December.

Kent Kanetsuna's art first came in Japan as Magnezone 093/DP-P, given to visitors at the spring 2008 Battle Road tournaments in March 2008.

A holofoil Dusknoir from the Stormfront three-pack blister, released with Stormfront in November 2008 with two Stormfront booster packs, one Secret Wonders pack and a Dialga or Palkia coin. The other blister held Magnezone DP32.

Kent Kanetsuna's art first came in Japan as Dusknoir 094/DP-P, a prize for players who got past the preliminary round of the spring 2008 Battle Road tournaments. Japan reprinted it in April 2009 in the Mewtwo LV.X Collection Pack, which gathered earlier event promos so that Japanese players could use them.

A holofoil Drifblim from the Stormfront two-pack blister, sold from late 2008 at stores such as Target and Wal-Mart with one Stormfront booster pack and one POP Series 7 pack. It reprints the Diamond & Pearl Drifblim with a new drawing by the same artist, Mitsuhiro Arita. That drawing first came in Japan as Drifblim 031/DP-P, from a McDonald's promotion in May 2007.

A holofoil Porygon-Z from the Platinum three-pack blister, made for Platinum's release on 11 February 2009 with two Platinum booster packs, one older pack and a coin showing Electivire and Magmortar. The other blister held Gliscor DP36. The blisters went on sale in Europe, but reached American stores nearly two months late, at the start of April.

Kagemaru Himeno's art first came in Japan as Porygon-Z 106/DP-P, in a Moonlit Pursuit and Dawn Dash special pack of July 2008.

A holofoil Gliscor from the Platinum three-pack blister, made for Platinum's release on 11 February 2009 with two Platinum booster packs, one older pack and a coin showing Electivire and Magmortar. The other blister held Porygon-Z DP35. The blisters went on sale in Europe, but reached American stores nearly two months late, at the start of April.

Kagemaru Himeno's art first came in Japan as Gliscor 108/DP-P, in a Cry from the Mysterious and Temple of Anger special pack of July 2008, alongside Dialga LV.X 107/DP-P, the later English DP37.

A holofoil Dialga LV.X from the 2009 spring Collector's Tins, released on 2 March 2009 with two Platinum booster packs, one Stormfront pack and one Secret Wonders pack. The other tins held Giratina LV.X DP38 and Shaymin LV.X DP39: all three Pokémon star in the film Giratina and the Sky Warrior. Ads promised a Pokémon Trading Figure Game figure in each tin, but delays kept the figures out.

It reprints the Great Encounters Dialga LV.X for the second time as a promo, after DP17 in 2008, again with a new drawing by Ryo Ueda. This drawing first came in Japan as Dialga LV.X 107/DP-P, in a Cry from the Mysterious and Temple of Anger special pack of July 2008.

A holofoil Giratina LV.X in its Origin Forme from the 2009 spring Collector's Tins, released on 2 March 2009 with two Platinum booster packs, one Stormfront pack and one Secret Wonders pack. The tins' three Pokémon, Dialga, Giratina and Shaymin, star in the film Giratina and the Sky Warrior. Ads promised a Pokémon Trading Figure Game figure in each tin, but delays kept the figures out.

It reprints Platinum's Giratina LV.X with a new drawing by the same artist, Shizurow, made for the English tins. At the time no Japanese card had used it.

A holofoil Shaymin LV.X in its Sky Forme from the 2009 spring Collector's Tins, released on 2 March 2009 with two Platinum booster packs, one Stormfront pack and one Secret Wonders pack. Ads promised a Pokémon Trading Figure Game figure in each tin, but delays kept the figures out.

It reprints Platinum's Shaymin LV.X with a new drawing by the same artist, Shizurow, made for the English tins. Japan got the drawing on 18 April 2009 in the Shaymin LV.X Collection Pack, one of three packs that brought the English tin art of Shaymin, Mewtwo and Regigigas LV.X to Japanese cards.

A holofoil Regigigas from the Regigigas Colossal Box of February 2009, which also held a jumbo copy of the card, three Platinum booster packs and two Diamond & Pearl series packs. The box was first announced as the Regigigas Premium Box, like the Darkrai, Dialga and Palkia boxes of 2008.

Kagemaru Himeno's art first came in Japan in the 11th Movie Commemoration Set of July 2008, made for the film Giratina and the Sky Warrior. English DP44 Magnezone and DP49 Dialga come from the same set.

tell.text: No foil anywhere on the card.

description.text: A non-holo copy was packed with a Pokémon DVD sold in the Netherlands in 2009. Like the non-holo Darkrai DP24 from The Rise of Darkrai DVD, it is one of a handful of European DVD promos that collectors rarely see.

description.text:
A holofoil Toxicroak G, Team Galactic's Toxicroak, packaged with the Platinum Player's Guide: a 140-page guide to every card of Platinum and Rising Rivals, released with Rising Rivals on 20 May 2009. The guide included a deck list built around the card.

Ryota Saito's art first came in Japan as Toxicroak G 008/DPt-P, an insert in the Galactic's Conquest Official Visual Book of October 2008.

A holofoil Carnivine G from the Rising Rivals three-pack blister, released with Rising Rivals on 20 May 2009 with two Rising Rivals booster packs, one Majestic Dawn pack and a coin. The other blister held Probopass G DP43. The English card prints its HP as "80 HP" rather than the usual "HP 80".

Makoto Imai's art first came in Japan as Carnivine G 001/DPt-P, the first card of the Platinum-era promo series. It was one of five promos handed out from October 2008 to people who bought two Galactic's Conquest packs at taking part stores.

A holofoil Probopass G from the Rising Rivals three-pack blister, released with Rising Rivals on 20 May 2009 with two Rising Rivals booster packs, one Majestic Dawn pack and a coin. The other blister held Carnivine G DP42. The English card prints its HP as "90 HP" rather than the usual "HP 90".

Ryota Saito's art first came in Japan as Probopass G 004/DPt-P, one of five promos handed out from October 2008 to people who bought two Galactic's Conquest packs at taking part stores.

A holofoil Magnezone from the Platinum Poster Pack of March 2009, sold at Best Buy with two Platinum booster packs, two POP Series 8 packs and a poster showing every Platinum card. It came out before DP41 to DP43, whose numbers stayed empty until May.

Kagemaru Himeno's art first came in Japan in the 11th Movie Commemoration Set of July 2008, where the card stands for Zero's Magnezone.

A holofoil Charizard G LV.X, Cyrus's Charizard, from the 2009 fall Collector's Tins, released on 2 September 2009 with two Supreme Victors booster packs, one Rising Rivals pack and one Diamond & Pearl series pack. The other tins held Garchomp C LV.X DP46 and Rayquaza C LV.X DP47. Some American tins were reported to hold German copies of the LV.X cards, probably a packing mix-up.

It reprints the Supreme Victors Charizard G LV.X, first printed in Japan's Garchomp vs Charizard SP Deck Kit, with a new drawing by the same artist, Wataru Kawahara, used only outside Japan.

A holofoil Garchomp C LV.X, Champion Cynthia's Garchomp, from the 2009 fall Collector's Tins, released on 2 September 2009 with two Supreme Victors booster packs, one Rising Rivals pack and one Diamond & Pearl series pack. The other tins held Charizard G LV.X DP45 and Rayquaza C LV.X DP47. Some American tins were reported to hold German copies of the LV.X cards, probably a packing mix-up.

It reprints the Supreme Victors Garchomp C LV.X, first printed in Japan's Garchomp vs Charizard SP Deck Kit, with a new drawing by the same artist, Shizurow, used only outside Japan.

A holofoil Rayquaza C LV.X, Champion Cynthia's Rayquaza, from the 2009 fall Collector's Tins, released on 2 September 2009 with two Supreme Victors booster packs, one Rising Rivals pack and one Diamond & Pearl series pack. The other tins held Charizard G LV.X DP45 and Garchomp C LV.X DP46. Cynthia is not known to own a Rayquaza: one appears with her only in a dream in an episode of the Diamond and Pearl anime.

It reprints the Supreme Victors Rayquaza C LV.X, first printed in Japan's Beat of the Frontier, with a new drawing by the same artist, Shizurow, used only outside Japan.

The last Tropical Wind, made for the 2009 Pokémon World Championships, held from 13 to 15 August 2009 at the Hilton San Diego Bayfront. Competitors received the card in seven languages, staff got a Staff copy, and the top finishers got copies stamped with their placement, from Top Thirty-Two up to Finalist.

Part of the print run carries the wrong number, DP25 (the 2008 card's number), instead of DP48. A collector on Elite Fourum reports that the error turns up on every version, the Finalist included.

description.text: A 2009 Top Sixteen copy printed with the wrong number, DP25 (the number of the 2008 card), instead of DP48. A collector on Elite Fourum reports a complete set in both the correct and the error printing.

description.text:
A holofoil Dialga from the Supreme Victors Poster Pack, released with Supreme Victors in August 2009 with two Supreme Victors booster packs, two POP Series 9 packs and a poster showing every Supreme Victors card.

Kagemaru Himeno's art first came in Japan in the 11th Movie Commemoration Set of July 2008, where the card stands for the Dialga of the film Giratina and the Sky Warrior.

A holofoil Arceus from two products released with the Arceus expansion on 4 November 2009. The Arceus Poster Pack held it with two Arceus booster packs, two POP Series 9 packs and a double-sided Arceus poster. The Arceus Poster Box held five Arceus packs, the same poster and a jumbo copy of the card.

Kunihiko Yuyama's art first came in Japan as Arceus 041/DPt-P, handed out at cinemas showing the film Arceus: To a Conquering Spacetime in 2009.

tell.text: Cosmos foil whose dots and circles are blocky, as if made of pixels, not smooth.
The picture shines; the rest of the card doesn't. An oversized copy, several times a playing card's size.

description.text: A jumbo copy came only in the Arceus Poster Box. Unlike earlier English jumbos, which used a glossy holofoil, it is printed on ordinary holofoil card.

A holofoil Cresselia from the Arceus three-pack blister, released with the Arceus expansion on 4 November 2009 with two Arceus booster packs, one Mysterious Treasures pack and an Arceus coin. The other blister held Darkrai DP52. Days later, the blisters seemed to be on sale only in Europe.

Wataru Kawahara's art first came in Japan as Cresselia 045/DPt-P, a prize for Pokémon Daisuki Club members who reached Super Rank with 3,200 action points. It was reprinted as 020/L-P when the LEGEND era began, and as many members only reached the rank after the change, the DPt-P print is the scarcer one.

A holofoil Darkrai from the Arceus three-pack blister, released with the Arceus expansion on 4 November 2009 with two Arceus booster packs, one Mysterious Treasures pack and an Arceus coin. The other blister held Cresselia DP51. Early product pictures showed a Majestic Dawn Darkrai in the blister instead of this card.

Wataru Kawahara's art first came in Japan as Darkrai 046/DPt-P, a prize for Pokémon Daisuki Club members who reached Super Rank with 3,200 action points. It was reprinted as 021/L-P when the LEGEND era began, and as many members only reached the rank after the change, the DPt-P print is the scarcer one.

A holofoil Arceus LV.X from the first, green Arceus Collector's Tin, planned for 2 December 2009 but brought forward to the Arceus expansion's release on 4 November. North American tins held three Arceus booster packs, two older Diamond & Pearl or Platinum series packs and one POP Series 9 pack; tins sold elsewhere held four packs.

It reprints the Arceus expansion's Arceus LV.X, first printed in Japan's Advent of Arceus, with a new drawing by the same artist, Shizurow, used only in English.

A holofoil Beginning Door printed only in French, as Porte de départ. It reprints the Trainer card from the Arceus expansion with the promo number DP54. France never got the Arceus expansion, whose Arceus cards came there as a sub-set of Supreme Victors, which may be why DP54 and DP55 were made only in French. Collectors found them in March 2010, months after DP53 and DP56.

In Japan the card first came in Advent of Arceus. A promo copy with that set's logo on the art was a prize at Advent of Arceus release events in July 2009.

Ultimate Zone with the promo number DP55, printed only in French, as Zone ultime. It reprints the Stadium card from the Arceus expansion, which lets Arceus decks move Energy around. France never got the Arceus expansion, whose Arceus cards came there as a sub-set of Supreme Victors, which may be why DP54 and DP55 were made only in French.

In Japan, Ultimate Zone first came as a promo with different art by Kent Kanetsuna, given with a comic about the Arceus decks to anyone who bought two Advent of Arceus booster packs when the set came out in July 2009.

A holofoil Arceus LV.X from the second, blue Arceus Collector's Tin, released on 16 December 2009 with two Arceus booster packs and two older Diamond & Pearl or Platinum series packs. The tin repeats the design of the first, green one, which held DP53.

It reprints the Arceus expansion's Meteor Blast Arceus LV.X, first printed in Japan's Arceus LV.X Deck: Grass & Fire, with a new drawing by the same artist, Ryo Ueda.
